items.text: No automated process anywhere in the files we have loads this table or its staging table. A separate catalog row proposes a manual spreadsheet upload as the source, but that row does not name this table directly and the connection is not confirmed by any code or data specific to this table

The location code in this table's business key is not formally linked to the store reference table, unlike the table's other three key columns, which are. Whether this has actually produced any location codes that do not match a real store was not measured, since checking would require an expensive scan across all 30 million rows

A single disabled reference to a similarly-named table was found and ruled out: a file validation utility carries commented-out code from 2014 for a file named SALES_DAILY_BUDGET_SNAP_F_DAT.csv, a different, snapshot-named table, alongside a header note from the same year recording that SALES_DAILY_BUDGET_F itself was decommissioned from that utility. The code path is disabled in all four files where it appears, not a live loader
The table and its staging table are both confirmed live and current: the staging table holds 371,872 rows today, and the target table's newest row is from this morning, hours before this analysis
This table carries no source-system tracking column of any kind, unlike most other tables in this project. Which system or process writes each row cannot be measured from the data here
No duplicate or invalid key values were found across all 30,164,433 rows

items.text: No automated loading process was found for this table, even though the table and its staging table are both confirmed live and current as of this morning. A manual spreadsheet upload is one working theory, but it is not yet confirmed
items.note: Confirming how this table is actually loaded would settle how it should be handled in the migration plan

items.text: Whether every location code in this table always matches a real store has not been checked directly
items.note: A manually entered location code is more likely than a system-generated one to occasionally not match a real store; confirming with the Weis team is cheaper than an expensive check across 30 million-plus rows

blocks.text: A few things below are still not fully confirmed. We are sharing this table's analysis now rather than holding it back, because the rest of it is solid and these gaps are clearly called out here, not hidden.

items.text: Still unknown: who gets notified if this process fails.
items.note: We could not find the program that loads this table anywhere in the files we have, so we have no way to see who is notified if it fails. A manual spreadsheet upload is one working theory, but it is not confirmed.

items.text: Still unknown: whether this process runs on a set schedule.
items.note: Same root cause as alerts: without the loading program itself, we have no way to confirm how often it runs.
